device.based_on: Original design around the 3340 VCO chip

architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic or 2-note paraphonic (two oscillators pitched independently through one filter, VCA and envelope set)
architecture.summary: 2 x 3340 VCOs with morphing wave shape + white noise + external input -> 12 dB/oct multimode filter (LP/BP/HP, dual output) -> overdrive -> VCA -> BBD delay -> output. Two ADSR envelopes, one audio-rate morphing LFO, sample and hold, slew limiter, two attenuators, mult, two summers and an inverter, all reachable on a 56-point patch bay with default (normalled) routings.

modules.name: MIDI / USB interface
modules.description: Converts MIDI (DIN or class-compliant USB) into per-oscillator pitch, gate, velocity, mod wheel, aftertouch and clock. Handles note priority, paraphonic allocation, key split, note range and poly chain.

modules.name: Pitch processing (portamento, bend, autoglide)
modules.description: Applies portamento, autoglide and pitch bend to the MIDI note for each oscillator, and adds the OSC1+2 CV input to both.

modules.name: Oscillator 1
modules.description: 3340 VCO. Five shapes that can be stepped or continuously morphed. Master when OSC SYNC is on.

modules.name: Oscillator 2
modules.description: 3340 VCO, identical to OSC 1. Slave when OSC SYNC is on.

modules.name: Noise generator
modules.description: White noise. Feeds the filter via the NOISE knob and is the default sample and hold source.

modules.name: External audio input
modules.description: Rear-panel mono input summed into the filter with the oscillators and noise. No level control.

modules.name: Oscillator mix and filter input sum
modules.description: OSC MIX crossfades the two oscillators. That result is summed with noise and the external input before the filter.

modules.name: Multimode filter
modules.description: 2-pole state-variable style filter with self-oscillating resonance. A second output carries a different mode from the main one.

modules.name: Overdrive
modules.description: Analogue soft-clipping stage with tone control, between filter and VCA.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Amplifier controlled by Envelope 1 by default. VCA BIAS holds it open without a gate.

modules.name: Bucket brigade delay
modules.description: Analogue BBD delay, 8192 stages. Can self-oscillate at high REPEATS depending on internal trimmer VR37.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Master volume and independent headphone amp.

modules.name: Envelope 1
modules.description: ADSR. Routed to VCA CV by default.

modules.name: Envelope 2
modules.description: ADSR. Routed to filter cutoff through ENV DEPTH by default, and to the inverter input.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Runs from 0.01 Hz to 10 kHz, so it doubles as an audio-rate modulator. Five shapes, stepped or morphed. Bipolar and unipolar outputs. Can sync to MIDI clock, retrigger per note, run one-shot, and track the keyboard.

modules.name: Sample and hold
modules.description: Samples its input on each clock and holds it. Internal clock set by RATE. GLIDE smooths the steps. Samples noise by default, giving random voltages.

modules.name: Slew rate limiter
modules.description: Limits the rate of change of any patched signal. Nothing is routed to it by default.

modules.name: Attenuator 1 (voltage controlled)
modules.description: Effectively a spare VCA. Level set by the knob and by the ATT1 CV input, which receives the ASSIGN output by default.

modules.name: Attenuator 2 (passive)
modules.description: Passive attenuator. By default it takes the LFO and feeds both pulse-width inputs, so its knob is the PWM depth.

modules.name: Multiple
modules.description: One input copied to two outputs. Carries the bipolar LFO by default.

modules.name: Sum 1
modules.description: Adds two signals or CVs.

modules.name: Sum 2
modules.description: Adds two signals or CVs.

modules.name: Inverter
modules.description: Inverts its input. Carries Envelope 2 by default.

modules.name: Assignable CV output
modules.description: DAC output that can carry one of five MIDI-derived values. Normalled into ATT1 CV.

parameters.function: Main output mode. Also determines the VCF 2 output mode (see filter.properties.second_output_mode).

parameters.label: RESO
parameters.function: Resonance. At or near maximum the filter self-oscillates as a sine at the cutoff frequency.

parameters.label: KEY TRK
parameters.function: Cutoff follows the latest MIDI note. Tracks well enough for the self-oscillating filter to be played as an oscillator.

parameters.label: TONE

parameters.label: LEVEL
parameters.function: Output level of the overdrive stage. Fully down silences the synth. Also sets how hard the delay is driven.

parameters.label: VCA BIAS
parameters.function: Minimum VCA opening, independent of the envelope. Turn up for drones or to hear external audio without a gate.

parameters.label: TIME
parameters.function: Delay time. Modulating short times gives chorus.

parameters.label: REPEATS
parameters.function: Feedback amount. At maximum the repeats are infinite and build up.

parameters.label: MIX
parameters.function: Dry/wet balance. Fully left is dry only, fully right is wet only.

ports.function: OSC 1 pitch CV. Adds to the MIDI pitch (inferred from patch tip 10).

ports.label: OSC 2

ports.label: FREQ MOD

behaviours.name: Envelope shape
behaviours.rule: Standard ADSR, 0 to 9 V. Attack is linear, decay and release are exponential. Gate threshold 1.5 V. Overlapping notes retrigger only if midi.envelope_retrigger is on.

behaviours.name: Filter cutoff sum
behaviours.rule: Effective cutoff = FREQ + FREQ MOD input x MOD DEPTH + Envelope 2 x ENV DEPTH + key tracking (if on) + MIDI mod source x VCF mod depth. Both depth knobs are positive only; use the inverter for negative envelope amounts.
behaviours.confidence: inferred from manual plus standard VCF practice

behaviours.name: Dual filter outputs
behaviours.rule: VCF 2 always carries a different response from VCF 1: HP -> BP, BP -> LP, LP -> HP. Summing VCF 1 and VCF 2 in LP mode (LP + HP) gives a notch.

behaviours.name: Self-oscillation
behaviours.rule: Near maximum RESO the filter outputs a sine at the cutoff frequency with no input. With KEY TRK on it can be played chromatically.

behaviours.name: Shape morphing
behaviours.rule: With blend on, SHAPE position p in [0,4] crossfades between shape floor(p) and floor(p)+1. With blend off it snaps to the nearest of five. Shape CV adds to the knob. Oscillator order: tone mod, pulse, saw, triangle, sine. LFO order: sine, triangle, saw, square, reverse saw (re-orderable).

behaviours.name: Pulse width
behaviours.rule: WIDTH only affects the tone mod and pulse shapes. Default PWM path is LFO -> ATT 2 -> both PW inputs, so ATT 2 is the PWM depth and patching PW1 or PW2 frees that oscillator from it.

behaviours.name: Hard sync
behaviours.rule: With OSC SYNC on, OSC 1 tracks the MIDI note and resets OSC 2's cycle. OSC 2 tuning or CV then changes harmonic content rather than pitch.

behaviours.name: Voice allocation
behaviours.rule: Mono: both oscillators play the priority note. Paraphonic: with two or more notes held the oscillators take different notes; with one note both play it. Key split: notes below the split go to OSC 1, the rest to OSC 2. Pedal mode: OSC 2 is frozen on one note. There is still one filter, one VCA and one envelope pair.

behaviours.name: Note range
behaviours.rule: Playable range is MIDI 24 to 96 by default. Notes outside are clamped to the nearest limit, or ignored if midi.mute_out_of_range is on.

behaviours.name: VCA control
behaviours.rule: VCA gain follows VCA CV (Envelope 1 by default) plus VCA BIAS. External audio is only heard while the VCA is open.

behaviours.name: Signal order and gain staging
behaviours.rule: Overdrive sits before the VCA, so distortion does not change as the note decays. Overdrive LEVEL sets how hard the delay is driven; hot levels plus high REPEATS push the BBD into distorted runaway feedback.

behaviours.name: Delay character
behaviours.rule: BBD delay, 25 to 640 ms. Feedback can exceed unity depending on trimmer VR37. Some clock noise is always present at long times. Modulating time shifts pitch, giving chorus at short settings.

behaviours.name: LFO modes
behaviours.rule: Free-running, or tempo-synced when MIDI clock is present. KEY SYNC resets phase per note (start phase per shape is settable). One-shot plays a single cycle per trigger. Key rate tracking scales rate by 2x per octave from a root note.

behaviours.name: Sample and hold
behaviours.rule: On each clock (internal RATE or external above 3 V) the input is sampled and held. GLIDE slews between values. Default input is white noise, giving stepped random voltage. The output goes nowhere until patched.

behaviours.name: Autoglide
behaviours.rule: Each note starts offset by up to +/-12 semitones and slides linearly to pitch at the PORTA TIME rate. Set per oscillator.

behaviours.name: Poly chain
behaviours.rule: All units on the same channel with poly chain on. Each unit plays the notes it can (1, or 2 if paraphonic) in played order and passes the rest down MIDI THRU. If the last unit has poly chain off it steals its voice for extra notes; if on, extra notes are dropped.

behaviours.name: Start-up calibration
behaviours.rule: Oscillators self-calibrate at power-on, so tuning is stable compared with the Model D. A model needs little or no drift.

behaviours.name: Patch bay semantics
behaviours.rule: Any output may be patched to any input. Inserting a cable into an input with a default source replaces that source. Inputs with 'combine: sum' add to the panel control instead. One output can feed several inputs via the mult.

transmits: sysex responses (software version, global setting updates)

main_commands.0A: global setting: 0A <sub> <value> (see parameters with access.type = sysex)
main_commands.10: ASSIGN output calibration (20 = 1 V, 21 = 4 V, 22 = down, 23 = up, 24 = save and exit)

omitted_from_source: firmware update and ASSIGN/BBD calibration procedures
tuning aid and software-version LED read-outs
example patches (worth adding later as test cases)
source_inconsistencies: Signal order: features text says the VCA passes through the overdrive; the routing table and block diagram say VCF > overdrive > VCA > delay. The table is used here, and patch tip 6 supports it.
ATT 2 default source is 'LFO (bipolar)' in the routing table and section 4.12, but 'uni-polar LFO' in the block diagram. Bipolar is used here.
LFO depth is 64 steps from 1 to 100% from the panel, but only 5 steps (20 to 100%) over SysEx.
Delay minimum is 24 ms in the overview and 25 ms in the specifications. Oscillator maximum is 'over 50 kHz' and 55 kHz.
SysEx table gives OSC sync and LFO key sync as '0 = enabled, 1 = disabled, default enabled'. This looks inverted relative to every other boolean and to the panel default.
SysEx VCF mod source has 4 values (disabled, aftertouch, mod wheel, velocity); the panel menu lists 5 slots including 'not used'.
Attenuator 1 description refers the reader to item 58 (VCA CV) where item 70 (ATT1 CV) is meant.
Rear output is a 'mono jack' in the text and 'TRS balanced' in the specifications. Both are true of a servo-balanced mono output.
Section 11.4 points to section 5.4 for tuning; tuning is section 5.5.
VCF mod source SysEx numbering differs from the ASSIGN numbering for the same three MIDI sources.

modelling_gaps.detail: Named and drawn as a pulse-like shape but not defined. Needs a scope capture.
Whether shape blending is a linear crossfade of adjacent shapes or something else is not stated. Shape CV volts-per-position is not given.
End points are given for most knobs (better than the Model D) but not the curve between them.
Inputs are rated -5 to +5 V but the effect per volt on cutoff, resonance, delay time, LFO rate and pulse width is not stated.
The manual does not say whether CV inputs without a default source add to the panel knob. 'combine: sum' is inferred.
Which oscillator takes the lower or newer note is not stated, nor behaviour with three or more notes.
Implied to be 100% (1 V/oct) since the filter can be played in tune, but not stated.
How the knob and ATT1 CV combine, and the CV-to-gain curve.
Clipping curve, gain range and tone filter corner frequencies are described only qualitatively.
BBD bandwidth, companding and filtering, which define the sound, are not covered. Feedback ceiling depends on a user-adjustable trimmer.
Not stated whether patching VCF IN removes noise and the rear input as well as the oscillators.
Described as post delay; whether it is also post VOLUME is not stated.
Resonance-versus-passband-gain behaviour and any input saturation are not described.
